info.title: Trinary Exchange API
info.description:
Public API for Trinary Exchange - the market data and enrichment layer for the EVE Frontier economy.

This API exposes four data domains:

- **Trading data**: order books, trades, price history, and market activity across Trinary Exchange trade hubs.
- **Keyspace enrichment**: decoded and contextualized on-chain state from the EVE Frontier world contracts.
- **Organization data**: Armature organizations, including governance structure, treasuries, and organizational units.
- **Frontier enrichment**: general reference data for EVE Frontier entities such as items, systems, and structures.

All requests are served through an authenticated gateway. Authenticate with the `x-api-key` header. Each operation's `x-cu-cost` is the Compute-Unit charge deducted per call.

get.description:
**Cost:** 150 compute units per request.

Live open orders across trade hub markets, ordered by last activity (newest first). Orders on hubs that no longer exist are excluded. Each row carries the hub display name (`hub_name`) and power state (`hub_state`, online/offline), so callers need not resolve them separately. All filters compose freely: scope by trade hubs (`storage_unit_ids`), by item (`asset_id`), by owner (`balance_manager_id`), and by side. Private-shared hubs are resolved by the caller — pass the hub list you can see; omit it for all hubs, or set `public_only=true` to restrict to location-revealed (public) hubs. Pagination is a single self-contained `cursor` param: pass `next_cursor` to page backward or `prev_cursor` to poll for new activity. Cursors embed the original filters, so no other params are needed (and filters are ignored) on cursor requests.

parameters.name: storage_unit_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated trade hub IDs and/or item collection IDs (max 100). Omit for all trade hubs.

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Numeric item type / asset id. Omit for all items.

parameters.name: balance_manager_id
parameters.description: Only orders owned by this balance manager ("my orders").

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Filter by order side (default: both). `buy` = bids.

parameters.name: public_only
parameters.description: Set `true` to restrict to location-revealed (public) assemblies. Omit for all visible hubs.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response (`next_cursor` for the next page, `prev_cursor` to poll for new activity). Self-contained: it carries the original filters and limit, so other params are ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (default and max 100).

get.summary: Unified open-orders discovery feed across trade hubs

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Net-to-seller display prices from the `display_price` view. Pass `item_ids` alone for vault-independent item-tier prices (one per item). Pass `item_ids` + `storage_unit_ids` to run the full traded → item → book → unknown waterfall per (item, vault); a pair with no pool falls back to the vault-independent item-tier price (`tier: "item"` with a null `pool_id`) unless `fallback=false`, and comes back `tier: "unknown"` when the item has no price anywhere. `storage_unit_ids` may hold either trade hub ids or vault item collection ids.

parameters.name: item_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated numeric item (asset) IDs. Batch ceiling: at most 100 IDs per request — larger batches are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: storage_unit_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated trade hub / vault item collection ids. When present, must match the number of `item_ids` (paired by position) or be a single id (applied to every item).

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Pair mode only. Set to "false" to disable the item-tier price fallback for pairs with no pool at the requested vault (default: enabled). Ignored in item-only mode.

400.description: Missing/non-numeric `item_ids`, more than 100 IDs, or mismatched `storage_unit_ids` length.

Returns the live order book for one item at a trade hub in a single request: resting bids and asks (bids highest-price-first, asks lowest-price-first), plus the resolved pool_id and pool metadata (asset names, decimals, taker fee) needed to price, size, and place orders against the book. Pass quote_type to prefer a market quoted in a specific currency. Responds 404 when the hub has no trading vault. When the hub trades but no market exists for this item yet, responds 200 with pool_id null and an empty book.

parameters.name: hub_id
parameters.description: Trade hub (storage unit) object ID

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Numeric item type ID

parameters.name: quote_type
parameters.description: Quote asset type string; exact matches are preferred.

parameters.name: hub_id

get.summary: Get vault configuration for a trade hub

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Authoritative current contents per storage, straight from the chain indexer — the spendable truth that overlay containers merely arrange. The whole read is scoped by `storage_unit_id`; the item collection is derived from it server-side. One call can read several storages at once: pass `owner_address` for the wallet warehouse, `balance_manager_id` for marketplace (balance manager) holdings, `vault_ids` for organization (DAO) receipt vaults, and/or `inventory_key` for the trade hub hangar (keyed by game `type_id`, not collection-scoped). Sections whose selector was not passed come back empty. All amounts are raw integers as decimal strings.

parameters.name: storage_unit_id
parameters.description: Trade hub scoping the whole read. The item collection is derived from it server-side (each hub backs exactly one collection), so no collection id is passed. A hub with no known collection fails with `404 not_found`.

parameters.name: owner_address
parameters.description: Holder wallet — returns warehouse balances.

parameters.name: balance_manager_id
parameters.description: Balance manager — returns marketplace balances.

parameters.name: vault_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated organization (DAO) receipt vault ids — returns per-vault balances.

parameters.name: inventory_key
parameters.description: Inventory field key (hub or character `owner_cap_id`) selecting which hangar — when passed, returns hangar contents (by type_id).

404.description: No item collection is known for `storage_unit_id` (`not_found`).

get.summary: Get authoritative inventory balances at a trade hub

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Returns hub locations currently offering the given item for sale, identified by type_id. Paginated: pass back `next_cursor` as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: item_id
parameters.description: The type_id of the tradeable item to filter by

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: cursor

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Same as `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}` but accepts up to 200 IDs at once via the `ids` query parameter. Returns one entry per requested ID, in request order; IDs that do not resolve return an entry with null fields and `metadata.error_reason = "unresolved"`. Results are cached per organization for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated organization object IDs (max 200).

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, or has more than 200 entries.

get.summary: Batch-get organizations by ID

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Returns top-level organizations (never their internal units) for a "discover organizations" listing. Each entry carries a member count as a size hint plus an icon and description when the organization has configured them. Sorted by member count (largest first) by default; pass `sort=name` for alphabetical. Paginate with `limit` and the returned `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of organizations to return (1–50).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response’s `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `members` (member count, largest first — the default) or `name` (alphabetical).

get.summary: List organizations for the discovery directory

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Resolves an organization object ID to the full organization: name, metadata, treasury and related object IDs, current members, and the complete tree of child units (`ous`). The ID may be the top-level organization or any unit within its tree — the top-level organization is always returned. Results are cached for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Object ID of the organization — the root organization or any unit within its tree.

404.description: No organization exists with the given ID.

get.summary: Get an organization and its full unit tree

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns every governance proposal of the organization, newest first: identity, lifecycle status, vote tallies, and — for composite proposals — the ordered step list. Per-proposal governance configuration and snapshot weights are not included; read those from the live on-chain object when hydrating a single proposal.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Object ID of the organization.

get.summary: List an organization's proposals

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns every keyspace the address can reach: keyspaces registered by one of the player’s organizations (`created`), keyspaces granted directly to the player (`player_grant`), and keyspaces granted to one of the player’s organizations (`ou_grant`). The player’s organizations are resolved automatically, so only the address is required. Results are cached for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Player wallet address.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Optional role filter (`grant`, `read`, or `write`). Narrows the grant-based matches; keyspaces the player’s organizations created are always included.

400.description: address param is missing, or role is not one of grant/read/write.

get.summary: List the keyspaces a player can access

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns every organization the address is a current governance member of, each resolved to its full unit tree. One entry per distinct top-level organization — inspect each tree’s per-unit `members` to see exactly where the address sits. Results are cached for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Player wallet address.

get.summary: List the organizations a player belongs to

Indexed replacement for the client-side registry dynamic-field walk. Returns { pool_id } for the given collection_id + asset_id (optionally preferring an exact quote_type match), or { pool_id: null } if no pool has been created yet.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: MultiCoin vault collection ID

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Numeric item type ID

parameters.name: quote_type

Returns pools and multicoin pools ranked by unclaimed fee balance (total deposited minus total withdrawn), descending. Only pools with a positive unclaimed balance are included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max number of results to return (default 20, max 100)

Returns enriched metadata for a pool including asset names, symbols, decimals, and the associated storage unit ID (for multicoin pools). Queries pools UNION multicoin_pools joined with warehouse_vaults.

parameters.name: pool_id
parameters.description: Pool (orderbook) object ID

Indexed replacement for the client-side versioned-inner dynamic-field walk. Returns { bids, asks } of resting orders (remaining_quantity > 0) from the materialized open_orders table. Bids are highest-price-first, asks lowest-price-first.

parameters.name: pool_id
parameters.description: Pool (orderbook) object ID

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns full detail for a single order — status, prices and quantities, the account that placed it, the trade hub it lives at, the market’s quote currency, and its fill history. Order IDs are scoped per pool, so both path segments are required. Responds 404 if the order is unknown to the indexer.

parameters.name: pool_id
parameters.description: Pool (order book) object ID the order belongs to.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order ID (u128, passed as a decimal string).

404.description: No order with this ID exists in this pool.

get.summary: Get one order on a pool
Compare the fuel, time, and balanced routes at once
get.description:
**Cost:** 300 compute units per request.

Runs the same search three times — once per optimization — and returns all
three routes, so a client can show the trade-off (fewer jumps versus less
fuel) without issuing three requests and without the results drifting apart
if the map reloads between calls.

This is three route calculations in one call and is priced accordingly;
prefer `/v1/routing/route` when only one optimization is needed. A 404 means
*no* optimization could connect the two systems under these parameters.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Solar system name to depart from (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Solar system name to arrive at (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: mass
parameters.description: Ship mass, in the game's mass units (default 1.0).

parameters.name: gate_weight
parameters.description:
How much to favour stargates over jump drives, 0.0–1.0, applied to the
`balanced` result (default 0.5).

parameters.name: max_jump_range_ly
parameters.description: Ship's maximum jump-drive range in light years (default 50.0).

200.description: All three routes for this pair

404.description: Unknown solar system, or no route between them

get.summary: Calculate a route between two solar systems
get.description:
**Cost:** 100 compute units per request.

Runs an A* search over the stargate network plus every jump-drive hop within
`max_jump_range_ly`, and returns the ordered waypoints together with the
route's jump counts and travel distance.

**Choosing an optimization.** `time` minimises travel time and will take long
jump-drive hops to skip gate chains. `fuel` minimises fuel burn and prefers
stargates, which are free but slower. `balanced` interpolates between them
using `gate_weight`.

**Ship parameters matter.** `mass` scales fuel burn per light year, so a
heavier ship shifts `fuel` and `balanced` results toward gates;
`max_jump_range_ly` bounds which drive hops exist at all, so a short-range
ship may be routed entirely over gates — or get a 404 when no gate path
exists.

**Reading the result.** `total_cost.total_jumps` is the hop count a player
sees; `gate_jumps` and `drive_jumps` split it by hop type;
`total_distance_ly` is the whole path and `drive_distance_ly` only the
jump-drive portion. A 404 means the systems are known but unreachable under
these parameters — retrying with a larger `max_jump_range_ly` may succeed.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Solar system name to depart from (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Solar system name to arrive at (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: optimization
parameters.description: Which cost to minimise: `fuel`, `time`, or `balanced` (default `time`).

parameters.name: mass
parameters.description:
Ship mass, in the game's mass units. Heavier ships burn more fuel per
light year, so raising this pushes `fuel` and `balanced` routes toward
stargates (default 1.0).

parameters.name: gate_weight
parameters.description:
How much to favour stargates over jump drives, 0.0–1.0, used only by
`balanced` (default 0.5). 0.0 behaves like `time`, 1.0 like `fuel`.

parameters.name: max_jump_range_ly
parameters.description:
Ship's maximum jump-drive range in light years (default 50.0). Jumps
longer than this are excluded from the graph before the search runs.

200.description: The optimal route under the given parameters

404.description: Unknown solar system, or no route between them

get.summary: Get routing graph coverage
get.description:
**Cost:** 20 compute units per request.

Reports the size of the stargate and jump-drive graphs the router searches.
Use it to sanity-check which map revision a client is routing against, and
to see the default `max_jump_range_ly` the jump-drive edges were built with.

**Cost:** 100 compute units per request.

Single search endpoint across characters and organizations. Matches `q` against character names, and against organization names, exact organization IDs, and exact treasury IDs. Use the `characters` and `orgs` flags to include either or both result groups (both are on by default). Each group is capped at `limit` results.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term: a partial name, or an exact organization / treasury ID.

parameters.name: characters
parameters.description: Include character results (default true).

parameters.name: orgs
parameters.description: Include organization results (default true).

parameters.name: limit

`/v1/hubs/nearby-by-system` to find trade hubs in the same neighbourhood.

Results are capped by `limit` (default 100, max 1,000) *after* sorting by
distance, so a large radius with a small limit returns the nearest systems
rather than an arbitrary subset.
